units.zh: 王殷，瀛州人。
units.en: Wang Yin was a native of Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Yin was a man of Ying Prefecture.

units.zh: 曾祖昌裔，本州別駕。
units.en: His great-grandfather Changyi had served as vice-prefect of that prefecture.
units.literal: His great-grandfather Changyi was vice-prefect of the prefecture.

units.zh: 祖光，滄州教練使，因家焉。
units.en: His grandfather Guang had been training commissioner of Cang Prefecture, and the family made its home there.
units.literal: His grandfather Guang was training commissioner of Cang Prefecture, and the family settled there.

units.zh: 唐末，幽、滄大亂，殷父鹹珪避地南遷，因投於魏軍。
units.en: When the Tang dynasty was nearing its end, You and Cang were thrown into chaos. Yin's father Xian'gui fled south to escape the fighting and threw in his lot with the Wei army.
units.literal: At the end of Tang, You and Cang fell into great disorder; Yin's father Xian'gui fled south to escape the turmoil and joined the Wei army.

units.zh: 殷自言生於魏州之開元寺，既長從軍，漸為偏將。
units.en: Yin himself said he had been born at the Kaiyuan Temple in Wei Prefecture. After he came of age he took up arms and slowly rose to become a field commander.
units.literal: Yin himself said he was born at the Kaiyuan Temple in Wei Prefecture; once grown he entered the army and gradually became a subordinate general.

units.zh: 唐同光末，為華州馬步軍副指揮使，因家於華下。
units.en: Near the end of the Tongguang era he was made deputy commander of Hua Prefecture's combined horse and foot forces, and he settled his household in the Hua region.
units.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang era he became deputy commander of the cavalry and infantry of Hua Prefecture and made his home below Hua.

units.zh: 天成中，移授靈武都指揮使，久之代還。
units.en: During the Tiancheng period he was transferred to command Lingwu. After a long tour of duty he was relieved and recalled.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was transferred and appointed commander of Lingwu; after a long time he was replaced and returned.

units.zh: 清泰中，張令昭據鄴叛，殷從範延光討之，首冒矢石，率先登城，以功授祁州刺史，尋改原州。
units.en: In the Qingtai period Zhang Lingzhao held Ye in rebellion. Yin marched with Fan Yanguang against him, took the lead under fire, and was the first to scale the walls. For this he was made prefect of Qi Prefecture, and before long was reassigned to Yuan Prefecture.
units.literal: During Qingtai, Zhang Lingzhao seized Ye in rebellion; Yin followed Fan Yanguang to attack him, was first to brave arrows and stones, and was first to scale the wall; for his merit he was appointed prefect of Qi Prefecture, and soon after was transferred to Yuan Prefecture.

units.zh: 殷性謙謹好禮，事母以孝聞，每與人結交，過從皆先稟於母，母命不從，殷必不往，雖在軍旅，交遊不雜。
units.en: Yin was by nature modest, careful, and devoted to propriety, and he was famed for the way he honored his mother. Before he kept company with anyone he always asked her leave; if she forbade it he would not go. Even amid camp life his circle of friends remained small and select.
units.literal: Yin's nature was modest, cautious, and fond of ritual; he was known for filial service to his mother. Whenever he formed friendships, his comings and goings were always reported to his mother first; if his mother did not approve, Yin would not go, and even in the army his associations were not mixed.

units.zh: 及為刺史，政事小有不佳，母察之，立殷於庭，詰責而杖之。
units.en: Once he became a prefect, the least slip in his governance would be noticed by his mother. She would have him stand in the courtyard, rebuke him, and beat him with a rod.
units.literal: When he became prefect, if there was the slightest fault in his administration his mother detected it, made Yin stand in the courtyard, questioned and reproached him, and beat him with a staff.

units.zh: 〈（《歐陽史》：殷為刺史，政事有小失，母責之，殷即取杖授婢仆，自笞於母前。）〉
units.en: (The 《Ouyang History》 records that when Yin was prefect and committed a minor error in office, his mother rebuked him; he immediately handed the rod to a servant and had himself beaten in her presence.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Ouyang History》: When Yin was prefect and there was a small lapse in his administration, his mother reproached him; Yin at once took the staff, handed it to a servant, and flogged himself before his mother.)〉

units.zh: 晉天福中，丁內艱，尋有詔起復，授憲州刺史，殷上章辭曰：「臣為末將，出處無損益於國家。
units.en: During the Jin Tianfu period he entered mourning for his mother. An edict soon recalled him to service and appointed him prefect of Xian Prefecture. Yin memorialized the throne to decline, writing: "Your servant is only a minor commander. Whether I serve or withdraw can neither help nor harm the state.
units.literal: During Jin's Tianfu era he was in mourning for his mother; soon an edict recalled him to office and appointed him prefect of Xian Prefecture. Yin submitted a memorial declining, saying: "Your servant is a low-ranking general; whether I take office or leave it brings no gain or loss to the state.

units.zh: 臣本燕人，值鄉國離亂，少罹偏罰，因母鞠養訓導，方得成人，不忍遽釋苴麻，遠離廬墓，伏願許臣終母喪紀。」
units.en: I am a man of Yan. My homeland was ravaged by war, and in youth I suffered exile and hardship; it was only through my mother's care and teaching that I grew to manhood. I cannot bring myself to cast off my mourning garments so soon or to leave her grave. I beg that I be permitted to see out the full mourning period for my mother."
units.literal: Your servant is originally a man of Yan; when my homeland was torn by disorder I suffered partial punishment in youth, and only through my mother's rearing and instruction did I become an adult. I cannot bear abruptly to cast off my hemp mourning garments and leave my mother's grave far behind. I humbly beg that I be allowed to complete the mourning period for my mother."

units.zh: 晉高祖嘉而許之。
units.en: Emperor Gaozu of Jin was pleased and granted his request.
units.literal: The Jin Gaozu praised this and granted his request.

units.zh: 晉少帝嗣位，會殷服闋，召典禁軍，累遷奉國右廂都指揮使。
units.en: When Emperor Shaodi of Jin came to the throne, Yin's mourning had just ended. He was summoned to take charge of the palace guard and was eventually promoted to commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army.
units.literal: When the Jin Shaodi succeeded to the throne, it happened that Yin's mourning period had ended; he was summoned to command the palace guard and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the right wing of the Fengguo army.

units.zh: 漢祖受命，從討杜重威於鄴下，殷與劉詞皆率先力戰，矢中於首，久之，出折鏃於口中，以是漢祖嘉之。
units.en: When the founder of Later Han took power, Yin joined the campaign against Du Chongwei at Ye. Both he and Liu Ci fought in the van with desperate courage. An arrow struck him in the head; long afterward he spat out the broken tip. The Han founder was deeply impressed.
units.literal: When the Han founder received the Mandate, Yin followed the campaign against Du Chongwei below Ye; both Yin and Liu Ci fought at the fore with all their strength; an arrow struck his head, and after a long while he drew out the broken arrowhead from his mouth; for this the Han founder praised him.

units.zh: 乾祐末，遷侍衛步軍都指揮使，領夔州節度使，會契丹寇邊，遣殷領兵屯澶州。
units.en: Near the end of the Qianyou era he was made commander of the palace infantry and concurrently military governor of Kuizhou. When the Khitans raided the border he was sent to hold Chanzhou with his troops.
units.literal: At the end of Qianyou he was transferred to commander of the palace foot soldiers and concurrently made military governor of Kuizhou; when the Khitans raided the frontier he was sent to lead troops stationed at Chanzhou.

units.zh: 及李業等作亂，漢隱帝密詔澶帥李洪義遣圖殷，洪義懼不克，反以變告殷，殷與洪義同遣人至鄴，請太祖赴內難。
units.en: When Li Ye and his faction rebelled, the Hidden Emperor of Han secretly ordered Li Hongyi, commander at Chanzhou, to move against Yin. Hongyi, fearing failure, instead warned Yin of the plot. Yin and Hongyi together sent envoys to Ye asking Taizu to come to the capital's aid.
units.literal: When Li Ye and others rose in rebellion, the Han Yindi secretly ordered the Chanzhou commander Li Hongyi to plot against Yin; Hongyi feared he could not succeed and instead reported the plot to Yin; Yin and Hongyi together sent men to Ye to ask the Taizu to come to the inner crisis.

units.zh: 殷從平京師，授侍衛親軍都指揮使。
units.en: Yin took part in pacifying the capital and was appointed commander of the palace guard.
units.literal: Yin followed in pacifying the capital and was appointed commander of the palace personal army.

units.zh: 太祖即位，授天雄軍節度使，加同平章事，典軍如故。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne, Yin was made military governor of the Tianxiong army and granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, while retaining command of the army as before.
units.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, Yin was appointed military governor of the Tianxiong army, given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and continued to command the army as before.

units.zh: 殷赴鎮，以侍衛司局從，凡河北征鎮有戍兵處，鹹稟殷節制。
units.en: When Yin went out to his command he took the palace guard staff with him. Every Hebei garrison under a military commissioner was placed under his authority.
units.literal: When Yin went to his post, the staff of the palace guard accompanied him; wherever in Hebei there were garrison troops at military commissions, all were placed under Yin's control.

units.zh: 又於民間多方聚斂，太祖聞而惡之，因使宣諭曰：「朕離鄴時，帑廩所儲不少，卿與國家同體，隨要取給，何患無財。」
units.en: He also extorted wealth from the populace on many pretexts. When Taizu learned of this he was displeased and sent word: "When I left Ye the treasury was well stocked. You and the state are one body—take what you need whenever you need it. Why should you lack for money?"
units.literal: He also levied money from the people in many ways; when the Taizu heard of this he detested it and had an envoy announce: "When I left Ye the treasury stores were not small; you and the state share one body—take what you need whenever you need it; why worry about lacking funds?"

units.zh: 二年夏，太祖征兗還，殷迎謁於路，宴賜而去。
units.en: In the summer of the second year Taizu returned from the Yan campaign. Yin met him on the road to pay his respects, was entertained and rewarded, and then went on his way.
units.literal: In the second year, summer, the Taizu returned from campaigning in Yan; Yin met and paid his respects on the road, was feasted and rewarded, and then departed.

units.zh: 及王峻得罪，太祖遣其子飛龍使承誨往鄴，令口諭峻之過惡，以慰其心。
units.en: When Wang Jun fell from favor, Taizu sent his son, the Feilong envoy Chenghui, to Ye with instructions to recount Jun's crimes to Yin by word of mouth and set his mind at ease.
units.literal: When Wang Jun fell into disgrace, the Taizu sent his son the Feilong envoy Chenghui to Ye with orders to tell Yin orally of Jun's faults and offenses in order to reassure his heart.

units.zh: 三年秋，以永壽節上表請覲，太祖雖允其請，且慮殷之不誠，尋遣使止之。
units.en: In the autumn of the third year he memorialized the court for an audience on the Yongshou festival. Taizu granted the request but doubted his sincerity and soon sent an envoy to forbid the journey.
units.literal: In the third year, autumn, on the Yongshou festival he submitted a memorial requesting an audience; although the Taizu granted the request, he also feared Yin was not sincere and soon sent an envoy to stop him.

units.zh: 何福進在鎮州，素惡殷之太橫，福進入朝，摭其陰事以奏之，太祖遂疑之。
units.en: He Fujin, stationed at Zhen Prefecture, had long resented Yin's overbearing ways. When Fujin came to court he laid out Yin's secret wrongdoing in a memorial, and Taizu began to suspect him.
units.literal: He Fujin was at Zhen Prefecture and had long detested Yin's excessive arrogance; when Fujin entered court he gathered Yin's secret misdeeds and memorialized them, and the Taizu then came to doubt him.

units.zh: 是年冬，以郊禋有日，殷自鎮入覲，太祖令依舊內外巡警。
units.en: That winter, with the suburban sacrifice approaching, Yin came in from his command to attend court. Taizu restored him to his former duties of internal and external patrol.
units.literal: That winter, with the suburban sacrifice drawing near, Yin came from his post to attend court; the Taizu ordered him to resume internal and external patrol duty as before.

units.zh: 殷出入部從不下數百人，又以儀形魁偉，觀者無不聳然。
units.en: Whenever he went abroad his escort numbered no fewer than several hundred men. His towering frame made every onlooker stand in awe.
units.literal: When Yin went out or in his retinue was never fewer than several hundred men, and because his bearing was tall and imposing, onlookers were all struck with awe.

units.zh: 一日，遽入奏曰：「郊禮在近，兵民大集，臣城外防警，請量給甲仗，以備非常。」
units.en: One day he rushed in to report: "The suburban rites are close at hand, and troops and civilians are assembling in great numbers. Your servant stands guard outside the walls. I ask that arms and armor be issued in due measure against any emergency."
units.literal: One day he suddenly entered and memorialized: "The suburban rites are near, soldiers and civilians are gathering in great numbers, and your servant is on guard outside the city; I request that arms and armor be issued in measured amounts to prepare for the unexpected."

units.zh: 太祖難之。
units.en: Taizu was troubled by the request.
units.literal: The Taizu found this difficult.

units.zh: 時中外以太祖嬰疾，步履稍難，多不視朝，俯逼郊禋，殷有震主之勢，頗憂之。
units.en: At the time, because Taizu was ill and walked with difficulty, he seldom held court. With the suburban sacrifice near at hand, Yin had grown so formidable that he seemed to overshadow his sovereign, and many at court were deeply uneasy.
units.literal: At that time inside and outside the court, because the Taizu was afflicted with illness and his steps were somewhat difficult, he often did not hold court; with the suburban sacrifice pressing near, Yin had the power to awe his ruler, and many were greatly worried.

units.zh: 太祖乃力疾坐於滋德殿，殷入起居，即命執之，尋降制流竄，及出都城，遽殺之，眾情乃安。
units.en: Taizu then dragged himself, despite his illness, to the Zide Hall. When Yin came in to pay his respects he was seized on the spot. An edict soon ordered him into exile, and as soon as he had left the capital he was put to death. Only then did public anxiety subside.
units.literal: The Taizu then, forcing himself despite illness, sat in the Zide Hall; when Yin entered to inquire after his health he was at once ordered seized; soon an edict was issued banishing him in exile, and once he had left the capital he was suddenly killed, and public sentiment then settled.

units.zh: 是歲春末，鄴城寺鐘懸絕而落，又火光出幡竿之上。
units.en: Late that spring the temple bell at Ye City snapped its ropes and crashed down, and flames were seen leaping from the top of a banner pole.
units.literal: At the end of spring that year, the temple bell at Ye City broke its suspension and fell, and again a blaze of fire appeared atop the banner pole.

units.zh: 殷之入覲也，都人餞於離亭，上馬失鐙，翻墮於地，人訝其不祥，果及於禍。
units.en: When Yin came to court the capital saw him off at the farewell pavilion. As he mounted his horse he lost a stirrup and fell to the ground. Onlookers took it for an evil omen—and disaster did indeed follow.
units.literal: When Yin came to court, the people of the capital saw him off at the parting pavilion; mounting his horse he lost a stirrup and tumbled to the ground; people marveled at the ill omen, and indeed disaster followed.

units.zh: 太祖尋令澶帥鄭仁誨赴鄴，殷次子為衙內指揮使，不出候謁，仁誨誅之，遷其家屬於登州。
units.en: Taizu soon sent Zheng Renhui, commander at Chanzhou, to Ye. Yin's second son, a commander of the inner guard, failed to come out to receive him. Renhui had him executed and sent the rest of the family into exile at Deng Prefecture.
units.literal: The Taizu soon ordered the Chanzhou commander Zheng Renhui to go to Ye; Yin's second son was a commander of the inner guard and did not come out to meet and pay respects; Renhui executed him and moved his family members to Deng Prefecture.

units.zh: 何福進，字善長，太原人。
units.en: He Fujin, whose courtesy name was Shanchang, was a native of Taiyuan.
units.literal: He Fujin, courtesy name Shanchang, was a man of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 父神劍，累贈左驍衛大將軍。
units.en: His father Shenjian was posthumously promoted several times to Grand General of the Left Qiaowei Guard.
units.literal: His father Shenjian was posthumously promoted several times to Grand General of the Left Qiaowei Guard.

units.zh: 福進少從軍，以驍勇聞。
units.en: Fujin took up arms in his youth and won renown for his boldness in battle.
units.literal: Fujin entered the army young and was known for fierce courage.

units.zh: 唐同光末，郭從謙以兵圍莊宗於大內，福進時為宿衛軍校，獨出死力拒戰於內，後明宗知而嘉之，擢為捧聖軍校，出為磁州刺史，充北面行營先鋒都校。
units.en: At the end of the Tongguang era Guo Congqian besieged Emperor Zhuangzong inside the palace. Fujin was then a night-guard officer and fought alone with desperate valor within the walls. When Emperor Mingzong learned of this he was pleased and promoted him to an officer of the Pengsheng army, made him prefect of Ci Prefecture, and appointed him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.
units.literal: At the end of Tang's Tongguang era, Guo Congqian surrounded Emperor Zhuangzong in the inner palace with troops; Fujin was then a guard officer of the night watch and alone exerted his utmost strength to resist and fight within; later Emperor Mingzong learned of this and praised him, promoting him to an officer of the Pengsheng army, sending him out as prefect of Ci Prefecture, and appointing him vanguard commander of the northern campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 清泰中，自彰聖都虞候率本軍從範延光平鄴，以功歷鄭、隴二州防禦使。
units.en: During the Qingtai period, as chief adjutant of the Zhangsheng army he led his troops with Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye. For his service he was made defense commissioner of Zheng and then of Long Prefecture in turn.
units.literal: During Qingtai, from chief adjutant of Zhangsheng he led his own army following Fan Yanguang to pacify Ye; for his merit he successively served as defense commissioner of Zheng and Long prefectures.

units.zh: 開運中，由潁州團練使入拜左驍衛大將軍。
units.en: During the Kaiyun period he came to court from his post as regimental trainer of Ying Prefecture and was appointed Grand General of the Left Qiaowei Guard.
units.literal: During Kaiyun he entered court from regimental trainer of Ying Prefecture and was appointed Grand General of the Left Qiaowei Guard.

units.zh: 屬契丹陷中原，令中朝文武臣僚凡數十人隨帳北歸，時福進預其行。
units.en: When the Khitans overran the Central Plains they compelled several dozen central-court officials to accompany the royal camp northward. Fujin was among them.
units.literal: When the Khitans overran the Central Plains they ordered several tens of civil and military officials of the central court to follow the encampment north; Fujin was then among those on the journey.

units.zh: 行次鎮州，聞北主已斃，其黨尚據鎮陽，遂與李筠、白再榮之儔合謀力戰，盡逐契丹，據有鎮陽。
units.en: When they reached Zhen Prefecture they learned that the Khitan ruler had died but his followers still held Zhenyang. Fujin joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and others in a fierce fight that drove the Khitans out completely and secured Zhenyang.
units.literal: When the party reached Zhen Prefecture they heard the northern ruler had died but his faction still held Zhenyang; they then joined Li Yun, Bai Zairong, and their kind in plotting and fighting with all their strength, completely driving out the Khitans and seizing Zhenyang.

units.zh: 時漢祖已建號於河東，詔以福進為北面行營馬步都虞候，尋拜曹州防禦使、檢校太保。
units.en: By then the founder of Later Han had proclaimed his rule in Hedong. He appointed Fujin chief adjutant of horse and foot for the northern campaign headquarters, and soon made him defense commissioner of Cao Prefecture with the acting title of Grand Guardian.
units.literal: At that time the Han founder had already established his title in Hedong; he decreed that Fujin be northern campaign chief adjutant of horse and foot, and soon appointed him defense commissioner of Cao Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 太祖出鎮於鄴，將謀北伐，奏以福進自隨。
units.en: When Taizu took command at Ye and prepared a northern campaign, he asked that Fujin accompany him.
units.literal: When the Taizu went out to command at Ye and planned a northern campaign, he memorialized that Fujin accompany him.

units.zh: 及太祖入平內難，以輔佐功拜忠武軍節度使，不數月，移領鎮州。
units.en: When Taizu marched in to settle the capital crisis, Fujin was made military governor of the Zhongwu army for his supporting service. Within a few months he was transferred to command Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: When the Taizu entered to pacify the inner crisis, for his supporting merit he was appointed military governor of the Zhongwu army; within a few months he was transferred to command Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 數年之間，北鄙無事。
units.en: For several years the northern frontier remained quiet.
units.literal: Within several years the northern frontier was without incident.

units.zh: 及聞太祖將有事於南郊，拜章入覲，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。
units.en: Learning that Taizu was to perform the southern suburban rites, he memorialized for an audience, was made military governor of the Tianping army, and was granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
units.literal: When he heard the Taizu would perform rites at the southern suburb, he submitted a memorial to attend court, was changed to military governor of the Tianping army, and given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 未及之任，卒於東京之私第，年六十有六，時顯德元年正月也。
units.en: Before he could take up the new post he died at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six, in the first month of the first year of Xiande.
units.literal: Before he could take up the post he died at his private residence in the Eastern Capital, aged sixty-six; it was the first month of the first year of Xiande.

units.zh: 累贈中書令。
units.en: He was posthumously promoted several times, ultimately to Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He was posthumously promoted several times to Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 子繼筠，仕皇朝，領建武軍節度使卒。
units.en: His son Jiyun served the dynasty and died while military governor of the Jianwu army.
units.literal: His son Jiyun served the imperial court and died while holding the post of military governor of the Jianwu army.

units.zh: 劉詞，字好謙，元城人。
units.en: Liu Ci, whose courtesy name was Haoqian, was a native of Yuancheng.
units.literal: Liu Ci, courtesy name Haoqian, was a man of Yuancheng.

units.zh: 梁貞明中，事故鄴帥楊師厚，以勇悍聞。
units.en: During the Liang Zhenming period he served under Yang Shihou, the former commander at Ye, and won fame for his fierce fighting.
units.literal: During Liang's Zhenming era he served under the former Ye commander Yang Shihou and was known for fierce valor.

units.zh: 唐莊宗入魏，亦列於麾下，兩河之戰，無不預焉。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang entered Wei, Ci entered his service as well. There was scarcely a battle fought between the two He rivers in which he did not take part.
units.literal: When Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong entered Wei he was also listed under his banner; of the battles between the two He rivers there was none in which he did not take part.

units.zh: 同光初，為效節軍使，轉劍直指揮使，尋以忤於權臣，出為汝州小校，凡留滯十餘年。
units.en: Early in the Tongguang era he was commissioner of the Xiaojie army and then commander of the Jianzhi guard. Soon, for offending a powerful minister, he was demoted to a petty officer at Ru Prefecture and languished there for more than ten years.
units.literal: At the beginning of Tongguang he was commissioner of the Xiaojie army, then transferred to commander of the Jianzhi guard; soon, for offending a powerful minister, he was sent out as a petty officer of Ru Prefecture and remained stuck there for more than ten years in all.

units.zh: 清泰初，詔諸道選驍果以實禁衛，由是得入典禁軍。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai period an edict ordered the circuits to select their boldest fighters to strengthen the palace guard. Through this Ci was able to enter palace service.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai an edict ordered the circuits to select fierce and able men to fill the palace guard; thereby he was able to enter and command the forbidden army.

units.zh: 晉初，從侯益收汜水關，佐楊光遠平鄴都，累遷奉國第一軍都虞候。
units.en: Early in the Jin period he followed Hou Yi in recovering Sishui Pass and assisted Yang Guangyuan in pacifying the Ye capital. He rose steadily to chief adjutant of the first Fengguo army.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin he followed Hou Yi in recovering the Sishui Pass, assisted Yang Guangyuan in pacifying the Ye capital, and was repeatedly promoted to chief adjutant of the first Fengguo army.

units.zh: 後從馬全節伐安陸，敗淮賊萬餘眾，晉祖嘉之，授奉國都校，累加檢校司空。
units.en: Later he joined Ma Quanjie in the attack on Anlu and routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels. The Jin founder was pleased and made him colonel of the Fengguo army, with repeated promotions to acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: Later he followed Ma Quanjie in attacking Anlu and defeated more than ten thousand Huai bandits; the Jin founder praised him, appointed him colonel of Fengguo, and repeatedly added the acting title of Minister of Works.

units.zh: 又從杜重威敗安重榮於宗城。
units.en: He also followed Du Chongwei in the defeat of An Chongrong at Zongcheng.
units.literal: He also followed Du Chongwei in defeating An Chongrong at Zongcheng.

units.zh: 及圍鎮陽，詞自登雲梯，身先士伍，以功加檢校司徒、沁州刺史。
units.en: During the siege of Zhenyang he climbed the assault ladder himself and led the charge at the head of his men. For this he was given the acting title of Minister of Education and appointed prefect of Qin Prefecture.
units.literal: When they besieged Zhenyang, Ci himself mounted the cloud ladder and took the lead before the ranks of soldiers; for his merit he was given the added acting title of Minister of Education and made prefect of Qin Prefecture.

units.zh: 時王師方討襄陽，尋命詞兼行營都虞候，襄陽平，遷本州團練使。
units.en: At the time the imperial army was campaigning against Xiangyang. Ci was soon made chief adjutant of the campaign headquarters as well. When Xiangyang fell he was made regimental trainer of that prefecture.
units.literal: At that time the imperial army was campaigning against Xiangyang; soon Ci was ordered concurrently to be chief adjutant of the campaign headquarters; when Xiangyang was pacified he was transferred to regimental trainer of that prefecture.

units.zh: 在郡歲餘，臨事之暇，必被甲枕戈而臥，人或問之，詞曰：「我以勇敢而登貴仕，不可一日而忘本也。
units.en: For more than a year in office, whenever he had a moment free from affairs he would sleep in armor with his weapon for a pillow. When asked why, Ci said: "I won my high office through courage. I must not forget that for a single day.
units.literal: In the prefecture for more than a year, in the leisure between affairs he would always wear armor and sleep with his weapon as a pillow; when people asked him, Ci said: "It was through courage that I rose to honored office; I cannot for a single day forget my origins.

units.zh: 若信其溫飽，則筋力有怠，將來何以報國也！」
units.en: If I grow used to comfort and ease, my strength will fail me. How then will I serve the state when it needs me!"
units.literal: If I trust in warmth and full belly, then sinew and strength will slacken—how in the future shall I repay the state!"

units.zh: 及漢有天下，復為奉國右廂都校，遙領閬州防禦使。
units.en: When Later Han held the realm he again became colonel of the right wing of the Fengguo army and held the post of defense commissioner of Lang Prefecture in absentia.
units.literal: When Han possessed the realm he again became colonel of the right wing of Fengguo and held Lang Prefecture defense commissioner in absentia.

units.zh: 從太祖平鄴，加檢校太保。
units.en: He followed Taizu in pacifying Ye and was given the acting title of Grand Guardian.
units.literal: Following the Taizu in pacifying Ye, he was given the added acting title of Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 乾祐初，李守貞叛於河中，太祖征之，朝廷以為侍衛步軍都指揮使，遙領寧江軍節度使，充行營馬步都虞候，命分屯於河西。
units.en: Early in the Qianyou era Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong and Taizu marched against him. The court made Ci commander of the palace infantry, military governor of the Ningjiang army in absentia, and chief adjutant of horse and foot for the campaign headquarters, with orders to encamp separately west of the river.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qianyou, Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong; the Taizu campaigned against him; the court appointed Ci commander of the palace foot soldiers, made him military governor of the Ningjiang army in absentia, and appointed him chief adjutant of horse and foot of the campaign headquarters, ordering him to station separately on the west of the river.

units.zh: 二年正月，守貞遣敢死之士數千，夜入其營。
units.en: In the first month of the second year Shouzhen sent several thousand suicide troops who raided Ci's camp by night.
units.literal: In the first month of the second year, Shouzhen sent several thousand death-defying warriors who entered his camp by night.

units.zh: 皆怖懼不知所為，惟詞神氣自若，令於軍中曰：「此小盜耳，不足驚也。」
units.en: The men were terrified and at a loss. Ci alone remained calm and ordered through the ranks: "These are only petty raiders. There is nothing to fear."
units.literal: All were terrified and did not know what to do; only Ci's spirit and bearing were as if nothing had happened; he ordered within the army: "These are mere petty bandits and not worth alarm."

units.zh: 遂免胄橫戈，叱短兵以擊之，賊眾大敗而退。
units.en: He doffed his helmet, seized his weapon crosswise, and drove the close fighters forward with a shout. The enemy broke and fled in rout.
units.literal: He then removed his helmet, took his weapon crosswise, shouted at the short weapons to strike them, and the rebel host was greatly defeated and withdrew.

units.zh: 自是守貞喪膽，不復有奔突之意。
units.en: From that day Shouzhen lost heart and no longer dared to launch sudden attacks.
units.literal: From this Shouzhen lost his courage and no longer had the will to make sudden raids.

units.zh: 河中平，太祖嘉之，表其功為華州節度使，歲餘，移鎮邢臺。
units.en: When Hezhong was pacified Taizu praised him and recommended his merit, appointing him military governor of Hua Prefecture. After a year he was transferred to command at Xingtai.
units.literal: When Hezhong was pacified the Taizu praised him and memorialized his merit, making him military governor of Hua Prefecture; after more than a year he was transferred to command Xingtai.

units.zh: 太祖受命，加同平章事。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne Ci was granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
units.literal: When the Taizu received the Mandate, Ci was given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 三年秋，改鎮河陽。
units.en: In the autumn of the third year he was transferred to command Heyang.
units.literal: In the third year, autumn, he was transferred to command Heyang.

units.zh: 顯德初，世宗親征劉崇，詞奉命領所部兵隨駕，行及高平南，遇樊愛能等自北退回，且言官軍已敗，止詞不行，詞不聽，疾驅而北。
units.en: Early in Xiande Emperor Shizong personally marched against Liu Chong. Ci was ordered to lead his troops with the imperial train. South of Gaoping he met Fan Aineng and others retreating from the north, who said the imperial army had already been beaten and urged him to halt. Ci would not listen and drove hard to the north.
units.literal: At the beginning of Xiande, Emperor Shizong personally campaigned against Liu Chong; Ci received orders to lead his own troops following the imperial carriage; when they reached south of Gaoping they met Fan Aineng and others returning from the north and saying the imperial army had been defeated; they tried to stop Ci from advancing, but Ci would not listen and spurred swiftly north.

units.zh: 世宗聞而嘉之，尋命為隨駕都部署，又授河東道行營副部署。
units.en: When Shizong heard of this he was pleased and soon appointed Ci overall commander of the imperial escort and deputy overall commander of the Hedong campaign headquarters.
units.literal: When Shizong heard of this he praised him; soon he was appointed overall commander accompanying the carriage, and also given the post of deputy overall commander of the Hedong circuit campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 其年夏，車駕還京，授永興軍節度使，加兼侍中，行京兆尹。
units.en: That summer, when the emperor returned to the capital, Ci was made military governor of the Yongxing army, given the concurrent title of Palace Attendant, and charged with the duties of metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.
units.literal: That summer, when the imperial carriage returned to the capital, he was appointed military governor of the Yongxing army, given the added concurrent title of Palace Attendant, and acted as metropolitan magistrate of Jingzhao.

units.zh: 二年冬，以疾卒於鎮，年六十有五。
units.en: In the winter of the second year he died of illness at his post, aged sixty-five.
units.literal: In the second year, winter, he died of illness at his post, aged sixty-five.

units.zh: 贈中書令，謚曰忠惠。
units.en: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat with the posthumous name Loyal and Kind.
units.literal: He was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat, and his posthumous title was Zhonghui, Loyal and Kind.

units.zh: 詞發身軍校，亟歷戎事，常以忠勇自負。
units.en: Ci had risen from the ranks as a military school officer and had seen much hard fighting, always priding himself on loyalty and courage.
units.literal: Ci rose from a military school officer and quickly passed through military affairs, always taking pride in loyalty and courage.

units.zh: 洎領藩鎮，能靖恭為治，無苛政以撓民，謚以忠惠，議者韙之。
units.en: Once he held a military commission he governed with quiet dignity and imposed no harsh measures on the people. That he was given the posthumous name Loyal and Kind met with general approval.
units.literal: When he came to lead a military commission he was able to govern with quiet respectfulness and had no harsh policies to trouble the people; to give him the posthumous title Loyal and Kind—discussants approved it.

units.zh: 子延欽，仕皇朝為控鶴廂使。
units.en: His son Yanqin served the dynasty as commander of the Konghe wing.
units.literal: His son Yanqin served the imperial court as commander of the Konghe wing.

units.zh: 王進，幽州良鄉人。
units.en: Wang Jin was a native of Liangxiang in You Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Jin was a man of Liangxiang in You Prefecture.

units.zh: 少落魄，不事生業，為人勇悍，走及奔馬，嘗聚黨為盜，封境患之。
units.en: In youth he was destitute and idle, fierce and fearless, and could keep pace with a galloping horse. He once led a band of robbers, to the dismay of the frontier district.
units.literal: In youth he was down and out and did not pursue any livelihood; he was brave and fierce by nature, could run as fast as a galloping horse, and once gathered a band to serve as bandits, which troubled the frontier district.

units.zh: 符彥超為河朔郡守，以賂誘置之左右。
units.en: When Fu Yanchao was a prefect in Hebei, he bribed Wang Jin and brought him into his retinue.
units.literal: Fu Yanchao was prefect of a commandery north of the Yellow River and, with bribes, lured him to keep him at his side.

units.zh: 長興初，彥超鎮安州，屬部曲王希全構亂軍州，令進賫變狀聞於朝廷，明宗賞其捷足，詔隸於軍中。
units.en: Early in the Changxing period Yanchao took command of An Prefecture. When his subordinate Wang Xiquan stirred rebellion in the army and prefecture, he had Jin carry an emergency report to court. Mingzong praised his swift feet and ordered him enrolled in the army.
units.literal: Early in Changxing, Yanchao commanded An Prefecture; when his subordinate Wang Xiquan stirred rebellion in the army and prefecture, he had Jin carry an emergency report to court; Mingzong praised his swift feet and ordered him enrolled in the army.

units.zh: 洎契丹內寇，戰於膠口，進獨追擒六十七人，時漢祖總侍衛親軍，知其驍果，擢為馬前親校。
units.en: When the Khitans invaded and battle was joined at Jiaokou, Jin alone pursued and captured sixty-seven men. The founder of Later Han then commanded the imperial guard; recognizing Jin's valor, he promoted him to personal attendant before his horse.
units.literal: When the Khitans invaded, at Jiaokou Jin alone pursued and captured sixty-seven men; at that time the Han founder commanded the imperial guard, knew his valor, and promoted him to personal attendant before his horse.

units.zh: 漢祖鎮河東，或邊上警急，令進賫封章達於闕下，自並至汴，不六七日復焉，由是恩撫頗厚。
units.en: When the Han founder held Hedong and border emergencies arose, he had Jin carry sealed memorials to the capital. From Bing to Bian and back took no more than six or seven days, and from this he won substantial favor.
units.literal: When the Han founder held Hedong, whenever the border was urgently alarmed he had Jin carry sealed memorials to the court; from Bing to Bian and back took no more than six or seven days, and from this his favor and care were quite generous.

units.zh: 繼任戎職，累遷至奉國軍都指揮使。
units.en: He continued in military service and rose through repeated promotions to commander of the Fengguo army.
units.literal: He continued in military office and was repeatedly promoted to commander of the Fengguo army.

units.zh: 從太祖入平內難，以功遷虎捷右廂都指揮使，歷汝、鄭防禦使，亦有政聲。
units.en: He followed Taizu into the capital to settle the internal crisis and was transferred for merit to commander of the right wing of the Hujie army. He served as defense commissioner of Ru and Zheng prefectures and also won a reputation for good governance.
units.literal: He followed the Taizu in entering to settle the inner crisis; for merit he was transferred to commander of the right wing of the Hujie army, served as defense commissioner of Ru and Zheng prefectures, and also had a reputation for good governance.

units.zh: 俄授相州節度使，為政之道頓減於前，議者惜之。
units.en: Soon he was appointed military governor of Xiang Prefecture, but his governing noticeably declined from before, to observers' regret.
units.literal: Soon he was appointed military governor of Xiang Prefecture; his way of governing abruptly declined from before, and discussants regretted it.

units.zh: 顯德元年秋，以疾卒於任。
units.en: In the autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness in office.
units.literal: In autumn of the first year of Xiande he died of illness in his post.

units.zh: 贈檢校太師。
units.en: He was posthumously granted the acting title of Grand Master.
units.literal: Posthumously granted Acting Grand Master.

units.zh: 史彥超，雲州人也。
units.en: Shi Yanchao was a native of Yun Prefecture.
units.literal: Shi Yanchao was a man of Yun Prefecture.

units.zh: 性驍獷，有膽氣，累功至龍捷都指揮使。
units.en: He was fierce and headstrong by nature, bold in spirit, and through repeated merit rose to commander of the Longjie army.
units.literal: His nature was fierce and unruly; he had daring spirit; through accumulated merit he reached commander of the Longjie army.

units.zh: 太祖之赴內難，彥超以本軍從。
units.en: When Taizu marched to settle the capital crisis, Yanchao followed with his own troops.
units.literal: When the Taizu went to the inner crisis, Yanchao followed with his own army.

units.zh: 國初，與虎捷都指揮使何徵戍晉州，會劉崇與契丹入寇，攻圍州城月餘，是時本州無帥，知州王萬敢不協物情，彥超與何徵協力固拒，累挫敵鋒。
units.en: Early in the dynasty he and He Zheng, commander of the Hujie army, garrisoned Jin Prefecture. When Liu Chong and the Khitans invaded they besieged the city for more than a month. The prefecture then had no military governor, and the prefect Wang Wang'an was unpopular. Yanchao and He Zheng held the city together in a stout defense and repeatedly drove back the enemy.
units.literal: At the beginning of the state, together with the Hujie commander He Zheng he garrisoned Jin Prefecture; when Liu Chong and the Khitans invaded and besieged the prefectural city for more than a month, at that time the prefecture had no commander; the prefect Wang Wang'an did not harmonize with popular sentiment; Yanchao and He Zheng joined forces to hold firm in resistance and repeatedly blunted the enemy's edge.

units.zh: 攻擊日急，禦捍有備，軍政甚嚴，居人無擾。
units.en: As the assaults grew fiercer by the day their defenses held firm, military discipline remained strict, and the townspeople were left unmolested.
units.literal: As attacks grew daily more urgent, their defense was prepared; military discipline was very strict, and the inhabitants were not disturbed.

units.zh: 及朝廷遣樞密使王峻總兵為援，敵兵宵遁。
units.en: When the court sent Wang Jun, commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, with relief troops, the enemy withdrew under cover of night.
units.literal: When the court sent the Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Wang Jun to command troops as relief, the enemy soldiers fled by night.

units.zh: 太祖嘉其善守之功，賞賜甚厚。
units.en: Taizu praised their skill in holding the city and rewarded them handsomely.
units.literal: The Taizu praised their merit in good defense and rewarded them very generously.

units.zh: 未幾，授龍捷右廂都指揮使，尋授鄭州防禦使。
units.en: Before long he was made commander of the right wing of the Longjie army and soon after defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.
units.literal: Before long he was appointed commander of the right wing of Longjie and soon after made defense commissioner of Zheng Prefecture.

units.zh: 劉崇之寇潞州也，車駕親征，以彥超為先鋒都指揮使。
units.en: When Liu Chong attacked Lu Prefecture the emperor marched in person and appointed Yanchao vanguard commander.
units.literal: When Liu Chong raided Lu Prefecture the imperial carriage campaigned in person and made Yanchao vanguard commander.

units.zh: 高平之戰，先登陷陣，以功授華州節度使，先鋒如故。
units.en: At the battle of Gaoping he was first over the walls and into the enemy line. For this he was made military governor of Hua Prefecture while retaining his post as vanguard commander.
units.literal: At the battle of Gaoping he was first to ascend and break the line; for his merit he was appointed military governor of Hua Prefecture while remaining vanguard as before.

units.zh: 大軍至河東城下，契丹營於忻、代之間，遙應賊勢，詔天雄軍節度使符彥卿率諸將屯忻州以拒之。
units.en: When the main army reached the walls of Hedong, the Khitans encamped between Xin and Dai in support of the enemy. An edict ordered Fu Yanqing, military governor of the Tianxiong army, to lead the generals to hold Xin Prefecture against them.
units.literal: When the great army reached below the Hedong city, the Khitans encamped between Xin and Dai, responding from afar to the rebel strength; an edict ordered the Tianxiong military governor Fu Yanqing to lead the generals to station at Xin Prefecture to resist them.

units.zh: 彥卿襲契丹於忻口。
units.en: Yanqing attacked the Khitans at Xinkou.
units.literal: Yanqing attacked the Khitans at Xinkou.

units.zh: 彥超以先鋒軍追蕃寇，離大軍稍遠，賊兵伏發，為賊所陷。
units.en: Yanchao pursued the enemy with the vanguard, drawing somewhat away from the main army. The enemy sprang an ambush and he was cut off and killed.
units.literal: Yanchao with the vanguard army pursued the barbarian bandits; separating somewhat from the great army, enemy troops sprang an ambush and he was trapped by the bandits.

units.zh: 世宗痛惜久之，詔贈太師，示加等也，仍命優恤其家焉。
units.en: Shizong mourned him deeply and decreed him posthumous Grand Preceptor—an exceptional honor—and ordered that his family receive generous care.
units.literal: Shizong grieved for a long time and decreed posthumous Grand Preceptor, showing an added grade, and still ordered generous relief for his family.

units.zh: 史懿，字繼美，代郡人也。
units.en: Shi Yi, whose courtesy name was Jimei, was a native of Dai Commandery.
units.literal: Shi Yi, courtesy name Jimei, was a man of Dai Commandery.

units.zh: 本名犯太祖廟諱，故改焉。
units.en: His original given name violated the taboo of Taizu's temple name, and for that reason it was changed.
units.literal: His original name violated the taboo of the Taizu's temple name, so it was changed.

units.zh: 父建瑭，事唐莊宗為先鋒都校，《唐書》有傳。
units.en: His father Jiantang had served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang as vanguard colonel and has a biography in the 《Tang History》.
units.literal: His father Jiantang served Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong as vanguard colonel; the 《Tang History》 has his biography.

units.zh: 莊宗之伐鎮陽，時建瑭為流矢所中而卒，懿時年甫弱冠，莊宗以其父歿於王事，召拜昭德軍使，俄遷先鋒左右廂都校，俾嗣其家聲。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhenyang, Jiantang was struck by a stray arrow and killed. Yi was then barely twenty. Zhuangzong, honoring his father's death in the state's service, summoned him and appointed him commissioner of the Zhaode army, and soon made him colonel of the left and right wings of the vanguard so that he might carry on his family's martial renown.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong campaigned against Zhenyang, at that time Jiantang was struck by a stray arrow and died; Yi was then just past weak-crown age; Zhuangzong, because his father died in royal service, summoned and appointed him commissioner of the Zhaode army, and soon transferred him to colonel of the left and right wings of the vanguard, enabling him to continue his family's renown.

units.zh: 天成中，為涿州刺史。
units.en: During the Tiancheng period he served as prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he was prefect of Zhuo Prefecture.

units.zh: 晉初，由趙州刺史遷洺州團練使，尋歷亳、鳳二州防禦使。
units.en: Early in the Jin period he was transferred from prefect of Zhao Prefecture to regimental trainer of Luo Prefecture, and soon served in turn as defense commissioner of Bo and Feng prefectures.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin he moved from prefect of Zhao Prefecture to regimental trainer of Luo Prefecture, and soon successively served as defense commissioner of Bo and Feng prefectures.

units.zh: 晉祖以其弟翰尚晉國長公主，故尤所註意。
units.en: Because Yi's younger brother Han had married the eldest princess of Jin, the Jin founder took special notice of him.
units.literal: The Jin founder, because Yi's younger brother Han married the Jin state's eldest princess, paid him especially close attention.

units.zh: 天福中，授彰武軍節度觀察留後。
units.en: During the Tianfu period he was appointed regent military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhangwu army.
units.literal: During Tianfu he was appointed regent military governor and observation commissioner of the Zhangwu army.

units.zh: 開運初，歷澶、貝二鎮節度使。
units.en: Early in the Kaiyun era, he served successively as military governor of the Chanzhou and Beizhou circuits.
units.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyun he successively served as military governor of the Chanzhou and Beizhou circuits.

units.zh: 三年，移鎮涇原。
units.en: In the third year he was transferred to command Jingyuan.
units.literal: In the third year he was transferred to command Jingyuan.

units.zh: 未幾，契丹入中原，時四方征鎮為契丹所召者靡不灊至，惟懿堅壁拒命，仍送款於漢祖。
units.en: Before long the Khitans overran the Central Plains. Of the military commissioners summoned by them across the realm, scarcely one failed to submit. Yi alone held his walls and refused their orders, while sending pledges of loyalty to the founder of Later Han.
units.literal: Before long the Khitans entered the Central Plains; at that time of the military commissions throughout the realm summoned by the Khitans there were none that did not slip in to submit—only Yi held his walls firm and refused orders, yet still sent pledges of loyalty to the Han founder.

units.zh: 漢有天下，就拜檢校太尉、同平章事，及賜功臣名號。
units.en: When Later Han held the realm he was at once made acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was granted a title honoring his merit.
units.literal: When Han possessed the realm he was at once appointed acting Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and was also granted a meritorious subject title.

units.zh: 廣順初，加檢校太師、兼侍中，進封邠國公。
units.en: Early in the Guangshun period he was given the acting title of Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Bin.
units.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he was given the added acting title of Grand Preceptor and concurrent Palace Attendant, and was advanced to Duke of Bin.

units.zh: 顯德元年春，以抱病歸朝。
units.en: In the spring of the first year of Xiande he returned to court, ill.
units.literal: In the spring of the first year of Xiande he returned to court because of illness.

units.zh: 〈（《東都事略·楊廷璋傳》：周太祖常諭廷璋圖涇帥史懿，廷璋屏左右，示以詔書，懿受代入朝，遂免禍。）〉
units.en: (The 《Eastern Capital Summary, Biography of Yang Tingzhang》 records that Zhou Taizu often directed Tingzhang to move against Shi Yi, commander at Jing. Tingzhang dismissed his attendants and showed him the edict. Yi accepted recall and came to court, thereby escaping disaster.)〉
units.literal: (The 《Eastern Capital Summary, Biography of Yang Tingzhang》: Zhou Taizu often instructed Tingzhang to plot against Jing commander Shi Yi; Tingzhang dismissed those at his side and showed him the edict; Yi accepted replacement and entered court, and thus escaped disaster.)〉

units.zh: 途經洛，卒於其第，年六十三。
units.en: Passing through Luoyang he died at his residence, aged sixty-three.
units.literal: Passing through Luo he died at his residence, aged sixty-three.

units.zh: 贈中書令。
units.en: He was posthumously made Director of the Secretariat.
units.literal: He was posthumously given Director of the Secretariat.

units.zh: 王令溫，字順之，瀛州河間人也。
units.en: Wang Lingwen, whose courtesy name was Shunzhi, was a native of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Wang Lingwen, courtesy name Shunzhi, was a man of Hejian in Ying Prefecture.

units.zh: 父迪，德州刺史，累贈太子太師。
units.en: His father Di had been prefect of De Prefecture and was posthumously promoted several times to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: His father Di was prefect of De Prefecture and was posthumously promoted several times to Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 令溫少以武勇稱，初隸唐莊宗麾下，稍遷廳直軍校。
units.en: Lingwen won early fame for his martial courage. He first served under Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang and was gradually promoted to a hall guard officer.
units.literal: Lingwen was known in youth for martial courage; he first served under Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and was gradually promoted to a hall guard officer.

units.zh: 明宗之為統帥，嘗與契丹戰於上谷，明宗臨陣馬逸，為敵所迫，令溫乃以所乘馬授明宗，而自力戰，飛矢連發，敵兵為之稍卻。
units.en: When Mingzong was supreme commander he once fought the Khitans at Shanggu. Mingzong's horse bolted under him on the field and the enemy closed in. Lingwen gave him his own mount and fought on foot, loosing arrow after arrow until the enemy drew back.
units.literal: When Mingzong was supreme commander he once fought the Khitans at Shanggu; Mingzong's horse bolted on the battlefield and he was pressed by the enemy; Lingwen then gave Mingzong the horse he was riding and fought on his own strength, loosing arrows in rapid flight, and the enemy soldiers for this drew back somewhat.

units.zh: 及明宗即位，歷遷神武彰聖都校。
units.en: When Mingzong took the throne, Lingwen rose to colonel of the Shenwu and Zhangsheng armies.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Lingwen was repeatedly promoted to colonel of the Shenwu and Zhangsheng armies.

units.zh: 晉初，自淄州刺史遷洺州團練使。
units.en: Early in the Jin period he was transferred from prefect of Zi Prefecture to regimental trainer of Luo Prefecture.
units.literal: At the beginning of Jin he moved from prefect of Zi Prefecture to regimental trainer of Luo Prefecture.

units.zh: 及安重榮稱兵於鎮州，晉祖以令溫為行營馬軍都指揮使，與都帥杜重威敗賊於宗城，以功授亳州防禦使，尋拜永清軍節度使。
units.en: When An Chongrong rebelled at Zhen Prefecture, the Jin founder made Lingwen commander of the campaign cavalry. With the supreme commander Du Chongwei he defeated the rebels at Zongcheng. For this he was made defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture and soon military governor of the Yongqing army.
units.literal: When An Chongrong raised troops at Zhen Prefecture, the Jin founder made Lingwen commander of the campaign headquarters cavalry; together with supreme commander Du Chongwei he defeated the rebels at Zongcheng; for his merit he was appointed defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture, and soon was made military governor of the Yongqing army.

units.zh: 屬契丹來寇，時令溫奉詔入朝，契丹遂陷貝州，其家屬因沒於契丹。
units.en: When the Khitans invaded, Lingwen was ordered to court. The Khitans then took Bei Prefecture, and his family fell into their hands.
units.literal: When the Khitans came to raid, at that time Lingwen received orders to enter court; the Khitans then captured Bei Prefecture, and his family members were thereby lost to the Khitans.

units.zh: 晉少帝憫之，授武勝軍節度使。
units.en: Emperor Shaodi of Jin took pity on him and appointed him military governor of the Wusheng army.
units.literal: The Jin Shaodi pitied him and appointed him military governor of the Wusheng army.

units.zh: 未幾，移鎮延州，又遷靈武。
units.en: Before long he was transferred to Yan Prefecture and then to Lingwu.
units.literal: Before long he was transferred to command Yan Prefecture, and again moved to Lingwu.

units.zh: 漢有天下，復為永清軍節度使，尋改安州。
units.en: When Later Han held the realm he again became military governor of the Yongqing army and soon was reassigned to An Prefecture.
units.literal: When Han possessed the realm he again became military governor of the Yongqing army, and soon was changed to An Prefecture.

units.zh: 國初，加檢校太尉、同平章事。
units.en: Early in the dynasty he was given the acting title of Grand Commandant and made co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
units.literal: At the beginning of the state he was given the added acting title of Grand Commandant and co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 世宗嗣位，遷鎮安軍節度使，罷鎮歸闕。
units.en: When Shizong came to the throne, Lingwen was made military governor of the Zhen'an army, then recalled from his post to court.
units.literal: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Lingwen was transferred to military governor of the Zhen'an army and left his command to return to court.

units.zh: 顯德三年夏，以疾卒，時年六十有二，詔贈侍中。
units.en: In the summer of the third year of Xiande he died of illness, aged sixty-two. An edict posthumously made him Palace Attendant.
units.literal: In the summer of the third year of Xiande he died of illness, aged sixty-two; an edict posthumously gave him Palace Attendant.

units.zh: 周密，字德峰，應州神武川人也。
units.en: Zhou Mi, whose courtesy name was Defeng, was a native of Shenwuchuan in Ying Prefecture.
units.literal: Zhou Mi, courtesy name Defeng, was a man of Shenwuchuan in Ying Prefecture.

units.zh: 初事後唐武皇為軍職。
units.en: He first served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang in a military post.
units.literal: He first served Later Tang's Martial Emperor in a military post.

units.zh: 莊宗之平常山，明宗之襲汶陽，密皆從征有功。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Changshan and when Mingzong raided Wenyang, Mi followed both campaigns with merit.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Changshan and when Mingzong raided Wenyang, Mi followed both campaigns with merit.

units.zh: 莊宗平梁，授鎮州馬軍都指揮使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Liang, he was appointed commander of the mounted army of Zhen Prefecture.
units.literal: When Zhuangzong pacified Liang, Mi was appointed commander of the mounted army of Zhen Prefecture.

units.zh: 明宗即位，累遷河東馬步軍副都指揮使。
units.en: When Mingzong came to the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Hedong mounted and infantry armies.
units.literal: When Mingzong took the throne, Mi was repeatedly promoted to deputy commander of the Hedong mounted and infantry armies.

units.zh: 晉天福初，除冀州刺史，累官至檢校司徒，入為右羽林統軍、檢校太保。
units.en: Early in the Jin Tianfu period he was made prefect of Ji Prefecture, rose through repeated offices to Acting Minister of Education, and entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard with the acting title of Grand Guardian.
units.literal: Early in Jin Tianfu he was made prefect of Ji Prefecture, rose through repeated offices to Acting Minister of Education, and entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard and Acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 四年秋，授保大軍節度使、檢校太傅。
units.en: In the autumn of the fourth year he was appointed military governor of the Baoda army and Acting Grand Tutor.
units.literal: In autumn of the fourth year he was appointed military governor of the Baoda army and Acting Grand Tutor.

units.zh: 屬部民作亂，密討平之，尋移鎮晉州，加檢校太尉。
units.en: When local people rebelled, Mi suppressed them. Soon he was transferred to command Jin Prefecture and given the acting title of Grand Commandant.
units.literal: When local people rebelled, Mi suppressed and pacified them; soon he was transferred to command Jin Prefecture and given the added Acting Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 開運中，入拜右龍武統軍。
units.en: During the Kaiyun period he entered court and was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Guard.
units.literal: During Kaiyun he entered court and was appointed commander of the Right Longwu Guard.

units.zh: 三年秋，出鎮延州。
units.en: In the autumn of the third year he went out to command Yan Prefecture.
units.literal: In autumn of the third year he went out to command Yan Prefecture.

units.zh: 其年冬，契丹陷中原，延州軍亂，立高允權為帥，時密據東城，允權據西城，相拒久之。
units.en: That winter the Khitans overran the Central Plains. The Yanzhou army rebelled and made Gao Yunquan commander. Mi held the eastern city and Yunquan the western city, and they opposed each other for a long time.
units.literal: That winter the Khitans seized the Central Plains; the Yanzhou army rebelled and set up Gao Yunquan as commander; at that time Mi held the eastern city and Yunquan held the western city, and they opposed each other for a long time.

units.zh: 會漢高祖建義於太原，遣使安撫，密乃棄其城奔於太原，隨漢祖歸汴，久居於闕下。
units.en: When Han Gaozu raised his standard at Taiyuan and sent envoys to reassure him, Mi abandoned his city and fled to Taiyuan. He followed the founder of Later Han back to Bian and lived long at court.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu raised his standard at Taiyuan and sent envoys to reassure him, Mi then abandoned his city and fled to Taiyuan, followed the Han founder back to Bian, and lived long at court.

units.zh: 廣順初，授太子太師致仕。
units.en: Early in the Guangshun period he was made Prince Tutor and retired from office.
units.literal: Early in Guangshun he was appointed Prince Tutor and retired.

units.zh: 顯德元年春卒，時年七十五。
units.en: He died in the spring of the first year of Xiande, aged seventy-five.
units.literal: He died in spring of the first year of Xiande, aged seventy-five.

units.zh: 長子銳，仕皇朝為內職。
units.en: His eldest son Rui served the dynasty in an inner-court office.
units.literal: His eldest son Rui served the imperial court in an inner-office post.

units.zh: 次子廣，歷諸衛大將軍。
units.en: His second son Guang rose to grand general of the guards.
units.literal: His second son Guang successively served as grand general of the guards.

units.zh: 李懷忠，字光孝，太原晉陽人。
units.en: Li Huaizhong, whose courtesy name was Guangxiao, was a native of Jinyang in Taiyuan.
units.literal: Li Huaizhong, courtesy name Guangxiao, was a man of Jinyang in Taiyuan.

units.zh: 父海，本府軍校。
units.en: His father Hai had been a military school officer of the Taiyuan command.
units.literal: His father Hai was a military school officer of the prefectural command.

units.zh: 懷忠形質魁壯，初事唐莊宗，隸於保衛軍。
units.en: Huaizhong was tall and powerfully built. He first served Emperor Zhuangzong of Tang in the Baowei army.
units.literal: Huaizhong's physique was tall and strong; he first served Tang's Emperor Zhuangzong and was attached to the Baowei army.

units.zh: 夾城之役，懷忠率先登城，以功補本軍副兵馬使。
units.en: At the siege of Jiacheng he was first over the wall. For this he was made deputy horse-and-weapons commissioner of his army.
units.literal: At the battle of Jiacheng, Huaizhong was first to scale the wall; for his merit he was appointed deputy horse-and-weapons commissioner of his army.

units.zh: 莊宗平定山東，累遷保衛軍使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, Huaizhong rose to commissioner of the Baowei army.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong pacified Shandong, Huaizhong was repeatedly promoted to commissioner of the Baowei army.

units.zh: 天成中，歷陜府、許州、滄州都指揮使，遙領辰州刺史。
units.en: During the Tiancheng period he served in turn as commander at Shaanfu, Xu Prefecture, and Cang Prefecture, and held the prefecture of Chen in absentia.
units.literal: During Tiancheng he successively served as commander of Shaanfu, Xu Prefecture, and Cang Prefecture, and held Chen Prefecture prefect in absentia.

units.zh: 清泰初，以河西蕃部寇鈔，命懷忠屯方渠。
units.en: Early in the Qingtai period, when the tribes of Hexi were raiding the borders, Huaizhong was ordered to encamp at Fangqu.
units.literal: At the beginning of Qingtai, because the tribal peoples of Hexi raided and plundered, Huaizhong was ordered to station at Fangqu.

units.zh: 晉祖受命，以懷忠故人，召典禁兵，三遷護聖左右廂都指揮使，遙領壽州節度使、檢校太保。
units.en: When the Jin founder took power he recalled Huaizhong, an old comrade, to command the palace guard. He was promoted three times to commander of the left and right wings of the Husheng army and held the posts of military governor of Shou Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian in absentia.
units.literal: When the Jin founder received the Mandate, because Huaizhong was an old acquaintance he was summoned to command the forbidden troops, was thrice promoted to commander of the left and right wings of the Husheng army, and held military governor of Shou Prefecture and acting Grand Guardian in absentia.

units.zh: 未幾，為同州節度使、檢校太傅。
units.en: Before long he was made military governor of Tong Prefecture with the acting title of Grand Mentor.
units.literal: Before long he became military governor of Tong Prefecture and acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 少帝嗣位，入為右羽林統軍，改左武衛上將軍。
units.en: When Shaodi came to the throne he entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard and was made senior general of the Left Wuwei Guard.
units.literal: When the Shaodi succeeded to the throne, Huaizhong entered court as commander of the Right Yulin Guard and was changed to senior general of the Left Wuwei Guard.

units.zh: 廣順中，以太子太傅致仕。
units.en: During the Guangshun period he retired with the title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: During Guangshun he retired with the title of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 三年夏卒，年六十六。
units.en: He died in the summer of the third year, aged sixty-six.
units.literal: In the third year, summer, he died, aged sixty-six.

units.zh: 詔贈太子太師。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: An edict posthumously gave him Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 白文珂，字德溫，太原人也。
units.en: Bai Wenke, whose courtesy name was Dewen, was a native of Taiyuan.
units.literal: Bai Wenke, courtesy name Dewen, was a man of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 曾祖辯。
units.en: His great-grandfather was Bian.
units.literal: His great-grandfather was Bian.

units.zh: 父君成，遼州刺史。
units.en: His father Juncheng had been prefect of Liao Prefecture.
units.literal: His father Juncheng was prefect of Liao Prefecture.

units.zh: 文珂初事後唐武皇，補河東牙將，改遼州副使。
units.en: Wenke first served the Martial Emperor of Later Tang as a Hedong guard general and was later made vice-commissioner of Liao Prefecture.
units.literal: Wenke first served Later Tang's Martial Emperor, was appointed a Hedong guard general, and was changed to vice-commissioner of Liao Prefecture.

units.zh: 莊宗嗣位，轉振武都指揮使。
units.en: When Emperor Zhuangzong came to the throne, Wenke was made commander of Zhenwu.
units.literal: When Emperor Zhuangzong succeeded to the throne, Wenke was transferred to commander of Zhenwu.

units.zh: 天成中，鎮州節度使王建立表為本州馬步軍都指揮使，遙授舒州刺史、檢校司空，歷青州、魏府都指揮使，歷瀛、蔚、忻、代四州刺史。
units.en: During the Tiancheng period Wang Jianli, military governor of Zhen Prefecture, recommended him as commander of horse and foot for that prefecture. He was given the acting title of Minister of Works and prefect of Shu Prefecture in absentia, then served as commander at Qing Prefecture and the Wei command, and in turn as prefect of Ying, Wei, Xin, and Dai.
units.literal: During Tiancheng, Zhen Prefecture military governor Wang Jianli memorialized that he be made commander of cavalry and infantry of that prefecture; he was appointed in absentia prefect of Shu Prefecture and acting Minister of Works; he successively served as commander of Qing Prefecture and the Wei prefectural command; he successively served as prefect of Ying, Wei, Xin, and Dai prefectures.

units.zh: 領代州日，兼蕃漢馬步都部署。
units.en: While he held Dai Prefecture he also served as overall commander of tribal and Han forces, horse and foot.
units.literal: On the days when he held Dai Prefecture he concurrently served as overall commander of barbarian and Han horse and foot.

units.zh: 漢高祖鎮並門，表為副留守、檢校太保。
units.en: When Gaozu of Han held Bingmen he recommended Wenke as deputy defender with the acting title of Grand Guardian.
units.literal: When Han Gaozu held Bingmen he memorialized that Wenke be made deputy defender and acting Grand Guardian.

units.zh: 漢國初建，授河中節度使、西南面招討使、檢校太傅。
units.en: When Later Han was first established he was made military governor of Hezhong, pacification commissioner of the southwest, and acting Grand Mentor.
units.literal: When the Han state was first established he was appointed military governor of Hezhong, pacification commissioner of the southwest, and acting Grand Mentor.

units.zh: 漢祖定兩京，改天平軍節度使，加同平章事。
units.en: When the Han founder secured the two capitals, Wenke was made military governor of the Tianping army and granted the title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.
units.literal: When the Han founder secured the two capitals, Wenke was changed to military governor of the Tianping army and given the added title of co-equal with the Secretariat and Chancellery.

units.zh: 未幾，鎮陜州，檢校太師。
units.en: Before long he was posted to Shaan Prefecture with the acting title of Grand Preceptor.
units.literal: Before long he commanded Shaan Prefecture as acting Grand Preceptor.

units.zh: 會河中李守貞叛，詔充河中府行營都部署。
units.en: When Li Shouzhen rebelled at Hezhong, an edict appointed Wenke overall commander of the Hezhong campaign headquarters.
units.literal: When Li Shouzhen rebelled in Hezhong, an edict appointed him overall commander of the Hezhong prefectural campaign headquarters.

units.zh: 時文珂已老，朝議恐非守貞之敵，乃命太祖西征。
units.en: Wenke was by then elderly, and the court feared he was no match for Shouzhen. Taizu was therefore ordered to campaign west.
units.literal: At that time Wenke was already old, and court discussion feared he was no match for Shouzhen; the Taizu was therefore ordered to campaign west.

units.zh: 河中平，文珂授西京留守、河南尹。
units.en: When Hezhong was pacified, Wenke was made defender of the Western Capital and metropolitan magistrate of Henan.
units.literal: When Hezhong was pacified, Wenke was appointed defender of the Western Capital and metropolitan magistrate of Henan.

units.zh: 太祖踐阼，加兼中書令，頃之，以太子太師致仕。
units.en: When Taizu took the throne, Wenke was given the concurrent title of Director of the Secretariat. Soon after he retired as Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
units.literal: When the Taizu ascended the throne, Wenke was given the added concurrent title of Director of the Secretariat; soon after he retired with the title of Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.

units.zh: 世宗即位，封晉國公。
units.en: When Shizong came to the throne, Wenke was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.
units.literal: When Shizong took the throne, Wenke was enfeoffed as Duke of Jin.

units.zh: 顯德元年，卒於西京，年七十九。
units.en: In the first year of Xiande he died in the Western Capital, aged seventy-nine.
units.literal: In the first year of Xiande he died in the Western Capital, aged seventy-nine.

units.zh: 輟視朝一日。
units.en: The court suspended audiences for one day in mourning.
units.literal: Court audiences were suspended for one day.

units.zh: 子廷誨，仕皇朝，歷諸衛將軍卒。
units.en: His son Tinghui served the dynasty and died after rising through the guard commands.
units.literal: His son Tinghui served the imperial court and died after successively holding posts as guard general.

units.zh: 白延遇，字希望，太原人也。
units.en: Bai Yanyu, whose courtesy name was Xiwang, was a native of Taiyuan.
units.literal: Bai Yanyu, courtesy name Xiwang, was a man of Taiyuan.

units.zh: 幼畜於晉之公宮，年十三，從晉祖伐蜀，以趫悍見稱。
units.en: He was raised from childhood in the Jin ducal palace. At thirteen he followed the Jin founder in the campaign against Shu and won praise for his fierce agility.
units.literal: He was raised young in the Jin ducal palace; at age thirteen he followed the Jin founder in campaigning against Shu and was praised for leaping fierceness.

units.zh: 晉有天下，歷典禁軍，累遷至檢校司空。
units.en: When Jin held the realm he served in the palace guard and rose to acting Minister of Works.
units.literal: When Jin possessed the realm he successively commanded the forbidden army and was repeatedly promoted to acting Minister of Works.

units.zh: 天福中，晉祖在鄴，安重榮叛於鎮州，帥眾數萬詣闕而來，晉祖命杜重威統諸將以禦之。
units.en: During the Tianfu period, while the Jin founder was at Ye, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhen Prefecture and marched tens of thousands toward the capital. The Jin founder ordered Du Chongwei to lead the generals against him.
units.literal: During Tianfu, when the Jin founder was at Ye, An Chongrong rebelled at Zhen Prefecture and led tens of thousands toward the capital; the Jin founder ordered Du Chongwei to command the generals to resist him.

units.zh: 時延遇不預其行，乃泣告晉祖，願以身先，許之。
units.en: Yanyu was not included in the expedition. He wept before the Jin founder and begged to lead the van in person. His request was granted.
units.literal: At that time Yanyu was not included in the expedition; he wept and told the Jin founder he wished to take the lead in person, and was permitted.

units.zh: 及陣於宗城，延遇率其屬先犯之，斬級數十，戰既酣，而劍亦折，諸將由是推伏。
units.en: At the battle line at Zongcheng he led his men in the first charge and took several dozen heads. In the heat of battle his sword snapped. The other generals were deeply impressed.
units.literal: When they formed battle lines at Zongcheng, Yanyu led his followers to strike first, beheading several tens; when the fighting grew fierce his sword also broke; the generals for this reason submitted to him in admiration.

units.zh: 晉祖聞之，即命中使以寶劍良馬賜之。
units.en: When the Jin founder heard of this he immediately sent a palace envoy with a precious sword and fine horses as rewards.
units.literal: When the Jin founder heard of this he at once ordered a palace envoy to bestow on him a precious sword and fine horses.

units.zh: 常山平，以功授檢校司徒，充馬軍左廂都校。
units.en: When Changshan was pacified he was given the acting title of Minister of Education and made colonel of the left wing of the cavalry.
units.literal: When Changshan was pacified, for his merit he was appointed acting Minister of Education and made colonel of the left wing of the cavalry.

units.zh: 後出為汾州刺史，遷復州防禦使。
units.en: Later he was made prefect of Fen Prefecture and then defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture.
units.literal: Later he went out as prefect of Fen Prefecture and was transferred to defense commissioner of Fu Prefecture.

units.zh: 國初，加檢校太保，尋受代歸闕。
units.en: Early in the dynasty he was given the acting title of Grand Guardian. Soon he was relieved and recalled to court.
units.literal: At the beginning of the state he was given the added acting title of Grand Guardian; soon he was replaced and returned to court.

units.zh: 屬太祖親征兗海，以延遇為先鋒都校，兗州平，授齊州防禦使。
units.en: When Taizu personally campaigned in Yanhai, Yanyu was made vanguard colonel. When Yan Prefecture fell he was made defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture.
units.literal: When the Taizu personally campaigned in Yanhai, Yanyu was made vanguard colonel; when Yan Prefecture was pacified he was appointed defense commissioner of Qi Prefecture.

units.zh: 歲餘，改兗州防禦使。
units.en: After a year he was reassigned as defense commissioner of Yan Prefecture.
units.literal: After more than a year he was changed to defense commissioner of Yan Prefecture.

units.zh: 在兗二年，為政有聞，人甚安之，州民數百詣闕，乞立德政碑以頌其美。
units.en: For two years at Yan his governance won wide praise and the people lived in peace. Several hundred residents went to court to ask that a stele be erected honoring his virtuous rule.
units.literal: For two years at Yan his governance was renowned; the people were greatly at ease; several hundred prefectural residents went to court requesting that a stele of virtuous administration be erected to praise his excellence.

units.zh: 顯德二年冬，世宗命宰臣李穀為淮南道軍都部署，乃詔延遇為先鋒都校。
units.en: In the winter of the second year of Xiande Shizong appointed Chief Minister Li Gu overall commander of the Huainan army and made Yanyu vanguard colonel.
units.literal: In the winter of the second year of Xiande, Shizong appointed chief minister Li Gu overall commander of the Huainan circuit army and decreed Yanyu vanguard colonel.

units.zh: 三年春，帥其所部與韓令坤先入揚州，軍聲甚振，尋命以別部屯於盛唐，前後敗淮賊萬餘眾。
units.en: In the spring of the third year he and Han Lingkun led their troops into Yangzhou first, and the army's fame spread far. Soon he was ordered to station a separate force at Shengtang and in repeated engagements routed more than ten thousand Huai rebels.
units.literal: In the spring of the third year he led his own troops with Han Lingkun to enter Yangzhou first; the army's renown was greatly stirred; soon he was ordered to station a separate division at Shengtang; before and after he defeated more than ten thousand Huai bandits.

units.zh: 四年夏，世宗回自壽春，制以延遇為同州節度使，未赴任，復命帥眾南征。
units.en: In the summer of the fourth year, when Shizong returned from Shouchun, an edict made Yanyu military governor of Tong Prefecture. Before he could take up the post he was ordered south again at the head of his troops.
units.literal: In the fourth year, summer, when Shizong returned from Shouchun, an edict made Yanyu military governor of Tong Prefecture; before he could take up the post he was again ordered to lead troops south.

units.zh: 是年冬，以疾卒於濠州城下。
units.en: That winter he died of illness below the walls of Hao Prefecture.
units.literal: That winter he died of illness below the walls of Hao Prefecture.

units.zh: 詔贈太尉。
units.en: An edict posthumously made him Grand Commandant.
units.literal: An edict posthumously gave him Grand Commandant.

units.zh: 唐景思，秦州人也。
units.en: Tang Jinsi was a native of Qin Prefecture.
units.literal: Tang Jinsi was a man of Qin Prefecture.

units.zh: 幼以屠狗為業，善角觝戲。
units.en: In youth he made his living as a dog butcher and was skilled in wrestling.
units.literal: In youth he made his living butchering dogs and was skilled at grappling contests.

units.zh: 初事偽蜀為軍校。
units.en: He first served the puppet Shu state as a military school officer.
units.literal: He first served the false Shu as a military school officer.

units.zh: 唐同光中，莊宗命魏王繼岌帥師伐蜀，時景思以所部戍於固鎮，首以其城降於繼岌，乃授興州刺史，為貝州行軍司馬。
units.en: During the Tongguang era Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Prince Jiji of Wei to lead an expedition against Shu. Jinsi was then garrisoning Gu Town with his troops and was the first to surrender the place to Jiji. He was made prefect of Xing Prefecture and campaign marshal of Bo Prefecture.
units.literal: During Tang's Tongguang era, Emperor Zhuangzong ordered Prince of Wei Jiji to lead troops against Shu; at that time Jinsi garrisoned Gu Town with his own troops and was first to surrender that town to Jiji; he was then appointed prefect of Xing Prefecture and made campaign marshal of Bo Prefecture.

units.zh: 屬契丹攻其城，因陷於幕庭，趙延壽素知其名，令隸於帳下，署為所部壕寨使。
units.en: When the Khitans attacked his town he fell into their hands. Zhao Yanshou, who had long known his reputation, took him into his service and appointed him trench-and-stockade commissioner under his command.
units.literal: When the Khitans attacked his town he fell into their camp; Zhao Yanshou had long known his name and had him attached under his banner, appointing him trench-and-stockade commissioner of his own command.

units.zh: 開運末，契丹據中原，以景思為亳州防禦使。
units.en: Near the end of the Kaiyun period the Khitans held the Central Plains and made Jinsi defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture.
units.literal: At the end of Kaiyun the Khitans held the Central Plains and made Jinsi defense commissioner of Bo Prefecture.

units.zh: 領事之日，會草寇數萬攻圍其城，景思悉力以拒之。
units.en: Soon after he took office, tens of thousands of bandits besieged the city. Jinsi resisted with all his strength.
units.literal: On the day he took office, tens of thousands of grass-bandits attacked and besieged his city; Jinsi exerted all his strength to resist them.

units.zh: 後數日城陷，景思挺身而出，使人告於鄰郡，得援軍數百，逐其草寇，復有其城，亳民賴是以濟。
units.en: Several days later the city fell. Jinsi went out in person, sent word to neighboring prefectures, and secured several hundred relief troops. He drove off the bandits, recovered the city, and the people of Bo were thereby saved.
units.literal: Several days later the city fell; Jinsi stepped forth in person, sent men to report to neighboring prefectures, obtained several hundred relief troops, drove off the grass-bandits, and recovered his city; the people of Bo thereby were saved.

units.zh: 漢初，改授鄧州行軍司馬，常郁郁不得志，後受代歸闕。
units.en: Early in Later Han he was reassigned as campaign marshal of Deng Prefecture. He remained depressed and unfulfilled, and was later relieved and recalled to court.
units.literal: At the beginning of Han he was changed to campaign marshal of Deng Prefecture, was often depressed and without fulfillment, and later was replaced and returned to court.

units.zh: 乾祐中，命景思為沿淮巡檢使，屢挫淮賊。
units.en: During the Qianyou period he was appointed inspector along the Huai and repeatedly defeated Huai rebels.
units.literal: During Qianyou he was ordered to be inspector along the Huai and repeatedly blunted Huai bandits.

units.zh: 時史宏肇淫刑黷貨，多織羅南北富商殺之，奪其財，大開告密之門。
units.en: At that time Shi Hongzhao abused the law and plundered the realm. He often framed wealthy merchants from north and south, had them killed, and seized their goods, throwing wide the door to secret denunciation.
units.literal: At that time Shi Hongzhao used excessive punishments and greedy seizure of goods; he often wove nets around wealthy merchants north and south, killed them, and seized their wealth, widely opening the gate of secret denunciation.

units.zh: 景思部下有仆夫，希求無厭，雖委曲待之，不滿其心，一日拂衣而去，見宏肇，言景思受淮南厚賂，私貯器械，欲為內應。
units.en: Among Jinsi's followers was a servant whose greed knew no bounds. Though Jinsi treated him with every consideration, the man was never satisfied. One day he stormed off and went to Hongzhao, accusing Jinsi of taking heavy bribes from Huainan, secretly hoarding arms, and plotting to act as an inside collaborator.
units.literal: Under Jinsi was a servant whose desires were insatiable; though Jinsi treated him with every consideration, he did not satisfy the man's heart; one day he shook out his robes and left, went to see Hongzhao, and said Jinsi had received heavy bribes from Huainan, secretly stored weapons, and intended to act as an inside collaborator.

units.zh: 宏肇即令親吏殿三十騎往收之，告者謂收吏曰：「景思多力，十夫之敵也，見便殺之，不然則無及矣。」
units.en: Hongzhao at once sent a trusted officer with thirty horsemen to seize him. The accuser told the arresting party: "Jinsi is immensely strong—the equal of ten men. Kill him on sight, or it will be too late."
units.literal: Hongzhao at once ordered a trusted official to lead thirty horsemen to seize him; the accuser told the arresting officers: "Jinsi is very strong—the match of ten men; when you see him kill him at once, otherwise it will be too late."

units.zh: 收騎至，景思迎接。
units.en: When the horsemen arrived, Jinsi came out to meet them.
units.literal: When the arresting horsemen arrived, Jinsi came out to meet them.

units.zh: 有欲擒之者，景思以兩手抱之，大呼曰：「冤哉！
units.en: When some moved to seize him, Jinsi seized one man in both arms and cried out: "This is injustice!
units.literal: When some wished to seize him, Jinsi embraced one with both hands and shouted loudly: "Injustice!

units.zh: 景思何罪？
units.en: What crime have I committed?
units.literal: What crime has Jinsi committed?

units.zh: 設若有罪，死亦非晚，何不容披雪？
units.en: If I am guilty, death will not come too late—why not let me clear my name first?
units.literal: If there is indeed a crime, death is not too late—why not allow the snow to be brushed away?

units.zh: 公等皆丈夫，安忍如此！」
units.en: You are all men of honor—how can you bear to act like this!"
units.literal: You gentlemen are all true men—how can you bear to act thus!"

units.zh: 都將命釋之，引告者面證景思，言受淮南賂。
units.en: The commander ordered him released and brought the accuser forward to confront Jinsi, who was accused of taking Huainan bribes.
units.literal: The commander ordered him released and brought the accuser face to face with Jinsi to testify that he had received Huainan bribes.

units.zh: 景思曰：「我從人家人並在此，若有十緡貯積，亦是受賂。
units.en: Jinsi said: "My followers and my household are all here. If you find so much as ten strings of cash laid by, call that a bribe.
units.literal: Jinsi said: "My followers and family are all here; if there is stored as much as ten strings of cash, that too would be taking bribes.

units.zh: 言我貯甲仗，除官賜外，有一事亦是私貯。」
